title: Two TAMIU students chosen for Texas A&M System Public Policy Scholars Program in Washington, D.C.
excerpt: Andrea Chapa Aguilar and Luis Maldonado Reyes will spend spring 2027 interning in Washington, D.C., through the Texas A&M University System Public Policy Scholars Program, according to TAMIU.
content:
Two Texas A&M International University students have been selected for the Texas A&M University System Public Policy Scholars Program, spending spring 2027 interning in Washington, D.C., while earning course credit, according to TAMIU.

The students are Andrea Chapa Aguilar, a junior political science major, and Luis Maldonado Reyes, a sophomore criminal justice major, the university said.

The program, made possible through the Texas A&M University System Office of Academic Affairs in partnership with the Public Policy Internship Program and the Bush School of Government and Public Service at Texas A&M University, places undergraduates from across the System in full-time, semester-long internships in Washington, D.C., according to TAMIU.

Aguilar said the experience fits her long-term goal of a career in law, where understanding how laws and policies work together is essential. Reyes, who is pursuing a concentration in Homeland Security, said the program bridges his studies with real-world work and fits his goal of a career in federal law enforcement, TAMIU reported.

Students in the program are expected to work full time at their internship placement, building skills, professional contacts and insight into their future fields, according to the university. TAMIU described the opportunity as part of its experiential-learning emphasis, which aims to help students apply classroom learning in real-world settings.

For more information on future public policy scholars opportunities, TAMIU lists QEP-LEARN director Cihtlalli G. Perez at CihtlalliG.Perez@tamiu.edu or (956) 326-2714.

Sources:

  • Texas A&M International University, “Two TAMIU Students Chosen for the Texas A&M University System Public Policy Scholars Program,” Oct. 29, 2026
